items.title: Albert Glenny Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: What sort of places did you play with Robert Charles' band?

ctx.x: I went out there with Lawrence. Morato. Morato. Morato. Morato. Yes, he's back. Huh? I know. He stopped playing with Joyce Lewis. I know. He was kind of his heart. Yes. I'm going to learn his part how to play bass. Bill Morato. Is that right? That boy, that old man with the bass player, he beat me. I don't say like somebody, I'm going to learn it. But that boy was a bass player. Yeah, that's just the truth, you know. The truth is the light. Sure.
Absolutely. Sure. What sort of places did you play with Robert Charles' band? Yeah. Yeah.

And Boston Club and Pickwick Club. What's the bass player name? The bass player name is bass. Pickwick, I told you all about that. Oh, love. Was this out near the Yacht Basin where you played? Oh, yeah. It was right across the- West End? No, that's the way you go on the West End, but we get to West End, there's a bridge across there. Bucktown? No, I'm a bridge. Oh, sure, let's come into New Bucktown. I mean, what Bucktown? It was a young bird. Oh, what's he cleaning up there?
